claims: The Purdue Boilermakers represent Purdue University in West Lafayette, Indiana.
The Purdue Boilermakers compete in NCAA Division I.
The Purdue Boilermakers are a Big Ten Conference member.
As of March 2026, Purdue University men's basketball team is advancing in the NCAA Tournament after a 79-77 win over Texas to reach the Elite Eight.
Purdue University men's basketball team has 26 Big Ten regular-season championships.
Purdue University men's basketball team has the most Big Ten regular-season championships in conference history.
Purdue University football plays at Ross–Ade Stadium.
Purdue University football produced NFL talent including Drew Brees.
Purdue University mascot is the "Boilermaker Special".
The "Boilermaker Special" is a 19th-century-style steam engine.
Purdue University nickname originated in 1891.
Purdue University nickname stems from the university's engineering roots.
Purdue University nickname stems from a 1891 football victory.
As of March 2026, Purdue University men's basketball team was the No. 2 seed.
Purdue University No. 2 seeded men's basketball team defeated No. 11 Texas 79-77.
Purdue University men's basketball team advanced to the Elite Eight by defeating Texas.
Purdue University men's basketball team was led by key performances from Trey Kaufman-Renn and Braden Smith.
Purdue University sports teams are not funded by student fees.
Purdue University sports teams operate independently.
